first_reasons.craft: Each pair crops to its change at true size, and the page stands 47,753 px at 1440 and 66,047 at 390. The quoted report words set 75 straight apostrophes and six straight quotes beside 181 curled ones (G3-S1). Item 4 asks approval for two colors and shows no swatch (G3-S2). Two text pairs cut a line through its middle or sit flush on the text (G3-S12).
first_reasons.clarity: Answer-first items, a numbered list and the reply line let Dustin say what each item asks. Item 3 prints "D03 and D04" bare (G3-S3), panel 3 reprints board 3's closed alternative replies as if they were open (G3-S4), and panel 2 carries studio words (G3-S10).
first_reasons.brand_fidelity: The chrome uses eight token colors with no Pillar Red or Prussian, and with the name covered the page reads as Oath & Action by Newsprint, Inter Tight and the status chips. Two recommendations fall short of the settled list: item 7's scope leaves out DR-204 and DR-36 (G3-M4), and item 6's change to Rule 05.5 leaves two chapter 05 rules applying the keyline the atlas target dropped (G3-M3). The header still sets the name in live type, as boards 2 and 3 did.
first_reasons.usefulness: Dustin can answer all eleven in about six minutes, and every link resolves: 21 on the page, 23 to version 14's rules. Item 6 asks him to approve words he cannot see (G3-M3).
first_reasons.evidence_honesty: Two projections for one page (G3-M1). Item 5's reason claims more than the check does (G3-M2). Item 6 says each change "makes the guide say one thing in one way", which change (c) does not achieve alone (G3-M3). Panel 6 rates chapter 14 at 76.7 percent of a figure set for chapter 14 with the kit (G3-S6), and panel 7's chapter 14 check ran an hour before version 14 was built (G3-S8).
first_reasons.accessibility: By the builder's run the wrapped copy passes the board check at 1440, 390 and 360 px: no type under 13 px, no low contrast, no sideways scroll, 40 focus stops with rings. All 48 pictures carry their size, lazy loading and an alt that says what the picture shows, and the 12 tables are live text in labeled, focusable scroll regions. The three luma alts name the conversion and leave out what it shows (G3-S5).

reasons.evidence_honesty: G3-M1 to G3-M3 are fixed: panel 6 labels both projections (15,180,545 as the build counts today; 15,650,545 with panel 2's allocations, 97.8 percent of 16 MB and 101.0 percent of the line), item 5 says band edges, item 6's reason now holds, and item 1 and panel 7 read the four-width file. G3-M1.title: Two projections for one page.
G3-M1.where: Panel 6, first table, the two rows "The page as projected with every chapter built" (15,180,545; 94.9 and 97.9 percent); panel 2, "Page weight", last paragraph ("puts the page about 150,545 bytes past the 15.5 MB line").

G3-M1.fix: Label panel 6's rows "as the build projects it today, with each Phase 4 chapter at 362,857 bytes", and add a row "with panel 2's allocations: 15,650,545 bytes, 97.8 percent of 16 MB and 101.0 percent of the 15.5 MB line", both read from the build report and panel 2's figures.

G3-M2.title: Item 5 promises more than the check does.
G3-M2.where: Panel 1, item 5's recommendation and its line under "The 11 items".
G3-M2.what: "so a later chart cannot run a line through its own label". The check is the kit's edge guard, which fails a band's edge drawn through a value label that a form marks for clearance (20261120_Label-Clearance-List.json, "what_this_is"; the engineer's A4 row). Panel 4's first line says so. A series line, an axis, a leader or another label crossing a word lies outside it, so "As proposed" approves a narrower guard than the sentence describes.
G3-M2.fix: "Switch it on for every chart, so no band's edge, such as a fan chart's range, can run through a value label." Add under "What it covers": "It tests band edges only; a line, axis or label crossing a word stays for the maker and the reviewer to catch."

G3-M3.title: Item 6 asks for changes to approved rules without their words, and change (c) leaves two rules saying the opposite.
G3-M3.what: Changes (a) and (b) have exact words in the register ("takes the text’s ink at any size", "The text’s ink, with the label (Rule 05.1)", "except a chip’s ID (Rule 18.24)"); the board prints a summary of each. Change (c) has no drafted words. Rule 05.3's reason says a working red mark on Newsprint "takes a keyline … (Rule 05.5)", and its rule names "where a reform acts" as a working red job. Rule 05.7, whose title covers charts and the atlas, gives the named point "a Charcoal keyline, as in Rule 05.5". With 05.5 alone changed, chapter 05 still says two things about the atlas target.
G3-M3.fix: Print each change as today's words beside the proposed words. The editor drafts (c)'s sentence for Rule 05.5 and the matching words for Rule 05.3's reason; for Rule 05.7, the same exception, or one line on why a chart's named point keeps its keyline. Name all three rules in (c).
G3-M3.owner: Editor (words), through the main session (report section 10 and the register row); builder rebuilds.

G3-M4.title: Item 7's scope leaves out two settled answers.
G3-M4.where: Panel 2, "What Phase 4 produces", rows 20 and 21, and "The checks Phase 4 runs"; panel 1, item 7.
G3-M4.what: DR-204 gives every screen product one dark mode, drawn from Night Edition on Charcoal, following the reader's device setting, with a visible switch that remembers the choice. Chapters 20 and 21 name no dark mode or switch, and no check captures one. Chapter 21 is "drawn from Concepts 03, 09, 10 and 11", the Master Brief's words from before DR-36, and the row never names the atlas visual system Dustin settled (DR-36, moved to Newsprint by DR-121) or its finishing list. Under gate rule 3, work outside an approved proposal waits for the next gate, so both need to sit in the words he approves.
G3-M4.fix: Chapter 20's row adds "every page on Newsprint and in the dark mode, with its switch". Chapter 21's row reads "in the atlas visual system you settled, on Newsprint, finished by its list, with views drawn from Concepts 03 Field Manual, 09 The Circuit, 10 Who Can Act and 11 Register". The checks add "Each web and atlas page in its dark mode at 1440 and 390 px, with the switch reached by keyboard and remembered". The reference line adds DR-36, DR-121 and DR-204.

phase_4_view.verdict: Approve it with additions. The engine is right: one application kit on the chart kit's model, drawn at build time, exports beside the guide, a dimension script and safe-area overlays, and the channel table holds DR-292's eight channels with every application Master Brief section 18 lists. As written it would produce applications at the right sizes in the right places; four gaps stand between that and finished work at the bar.
scope: Web (20): add the home page and one Act page at the four widths, and DR-204's dark mode with its switch (G3-M4).
Atlas (21): name DR-36's system and its finishing list (G3-M4).

Substack and email (22): one chart inside a post as a still image with alt and source line (DR-49, DR-59); the working email with a dark-mode pass, a plain-text part, alt on every image and HTML small enough that Gmail shows it whole (about 102 KB, for the research lead to confirm).

Social (23): each profile as a reader meets it, avatar over banner at desktop and phone width; S95's 1080 x 1920 frame held by DR-268; DR-116's avatar and DR-211's 96 px sign-off; the web address held as DR-55 set.

Reports and print (24, 25): the sizes Master Brief section 18 asks for (US Letter with bleed and margins, 24 x 36 in poster, 11 x 17 in table sign), the print lockup of DR-210, and DR-102 for an event piece with a host.

Photography (16): placeholders cannot teach a selection, crop or caption rule; a fifth question could let chapter 16 teach on two or three public-domain federal photographs, as chapter 01 does (DR-238), each with a rights row, while Q-04 stays open.
phase_4_view.allocations: The arithmetic holds: 3,359,455 bytes of room, 3,010,000 allocated (89.6 percent), 349,455 in reserve. The method sizes each chapter by its count of rules, and the two chapters with the most drawing get the thinnest margins: chapter 23 sits 0.4 percent above its own estimate (20 rules at 32,856) and chapter 20 2.8 percent (10 at 48,651); chapter 23's analog draws little and chapter 20's holds no dark mode. In chat 10, measure the kit's bytes for a social post, a web page at four widths with its dark mode and a report page, re-size the seven, and show it on Phase 4 board 1. Chapter 27's 200,000 must index every export.
